findings.evidence: evidence/R850/noroute_run1..3.json raw.physics; independent recompute per R847 method
findings.observation: #151 stop distances 0.1221/0.115317/0.115716 m and sim stop times 0.372/0.365/0.385 s reproduce; max 0.1221 m / 0.385 s; all ok=true, E_LOCAL_NO_ROUTE, 0.4 m/s; post-stop xy drift 0.0 over 4.3-5.5 s.

findings.evidence: same three raw runs; trigger lies between physics samples; interpolation and last-pre-trigger recompute
findings.observation: The reported distance starts at the first sample with wall>=trigger, omitting 7.5-11.6 mm of travel. Trigger-interpolated distances are 0.1311/0.1253/0.1232 m; from the last pre-trigger sample 0.1337/0.1273/0.1237 m. The 0.15 m budget still covers corrected max 0.1337 m (margin 0.0163 m, ~11%), not the claimed 23%; the reported 6.8 mm spread is a method artifact (true spread ~10.5 mm).

findings.evidence: raw.physics velocity profile run1; ws/src/95_simulation/lite3_gazebo_sim/src/lite3_planar_drive.cpp SetLinearVel; URDF driveMode=dynamic
findings.observation: The carrier is velocity-actuated: vx=0.4 at sim 1.550 (x=0.15602), vx=0.0 at sim 1.571 (x=0.16001), i.e. a one-sample (~4 mm) stop with no braking model. 0.1221 m is perception+local-planning+mux latency, not a braking-inclusive stop distance. The original R716/24 4.1 requirement explicitly asked for braking; 'Gazebo dynamics' and 'full_chain' overstate, and the chain excludes the global planner (R850 4.3 admits this).

findings.evidence: calibration.py FROZEN/PENDING_REQUIRED/SCOPED_REQUIRED/DIGEST; frozen_baseline.json; git diff 052f5e9..6a689be; leaf diff; check_loosening(old,new)
findings.observation: stop_time_s=0.50 and stop_distance_m=0.15 with the declared scope/sample_n=3/evidence; PENDING_REQUIRED=[]; both keys in SCOPED_REQUIRED with min_sample_n=3 and exact scope; DIGEST=4f570e94... matches calibration.digest(); baseline is deep-equal to FROZEN and digest matches; only the two keys were added, no other frozen value changed; check_loosening(round-2 FROZEN, HEAD FROZEN) returns [].

No unfreeze_log entry exists for budgets.stop_time_s.value or budgets.stop_distance_m.value. Every prior new key frozen from pending (cancel_time, brake peak, osmesa, p95_local, localization, success_rate) has a from='未定标（pending）'/to=value/reason record. R850 added two frozen keys silently, contrary to the module's explicit-unfreeze contract.

REQUIRED has no budgets.stop_time_s.* or budgets.stop_distance_m.* shape entries. With scope/sample_n/evidence present, validate_frozen returns status=pass and pending=[] when value is missing, None, or inf; only assert_digest catches those mutations. Missing evidence is caught by the ad-hoc loop. The new keys have weaker shape validation than every other frozen budget key.

For budget keys the guard flags a decrease as loosening and ignores an increase: 0.15->0.50 returns []; 0.15->0.10 raises E_CAL_LOOSENED. The test that documented this blind spot was deleted by R850 and still passes against current config. No remaining test covers a stop-budget raise.

findings.evidence: git diff 052f5e9..6a689be -- test_calibration.py; 33-suite run; re-executed deleted tests
findings.observation: Calibration tests shrank 59->52 (12 removed, 5 added); 8 deletions are collateral beyond the 4 stop/state replacements. 6 of the 8 still pass against current config; the other 2 fail only because they assert the obsolete blocked/pending=2 state. Deleted tests include test_budget_raise_not_flagged_by_loosening, test_stop_component_raise_logged, the p95_local guards, the osmesa guards, and resources/sampling shape checks. Total suite cases fell 314->308 (calibration -7, test_execution +1). R850.md/timeline say only the R716 test was replaced; this understates the shrinkage.

findings.evidence: local_native.py lines 197-201 at 6a689be; test_execution.py rename; R845 proof
findings.observation: The R842 hunk is gone: the zero-length branch again returns complete when now>=target[3], certifying contact from the clock alone. R845's unreachability proof covers plan() results only; no test pins the zero-length branch or enforces unreachability, and an external caller passing a zero-length trajectory could still hit it. The revert removed a hardening without a replacement guard.
test_in_flight_uncertainty_blocks_contact_certification fails (complete=True) when + uncertainty_m is removed and passes on HEAD. It protects the uncertainty term, not the zero-length step branch.
F5 collision count is 16 (all dynamic_collision, segment 3, samples=545), not 17; trace has 9 points, no execution_trace, old domain string. R845's correction is accurate.

R850 runs have top-level hardware=false; R845 a5_ros_v4_full.json has hardware=false only per case, no top-level hardware key, so G4 is only half closed.

Code blob/sha256 match R846 code_ref.

Retraction is honest: bad-batch world_feet_end max x 0.099-0.980 (<1.0), force_experiment=[] for the six force runs and None for the two pd runs; force070 vs pd070 have 32 identical phases. Valid force run has force_reports length 3; rear lifts 3.99/5.64/5.59 cm vs plain 8.11/8.37/8.96 cm, all force lifted=False and plain lifted=True. 0.04 m is a single low step, and R848 4.2 says so; R849's 'two-level/low step' shorthand is looser but the primary evidence is honest.
